name: Ambur Biryani
subtitle: seeraga samba rice and mutton with a soaked chilli paste, no whole garam masala at all

ingredients.note: seeraga samba is the authentic grain; basmati is the workable substitute

ingredients.qty: 15, soaked and ground to a paste
ingredients.note: the defining element; Ambur uses chilli paste, not powder

prepNotes: Ambur biryani has almost no whole spice. The flavour is chilli paste, ginger, garlic and mint, and the restraint is the point.
It is cooked as a one-pot dish, not layered. The rice goes into the meat stock.

steps.text: Marinate the mutton in the yogurt, ginger, garlic and half the chilli paste for 1 hour in the refrigerator.
Fry the onion in the oil until golden. Add the rest of the chilli paste and fry 3 minutes.
Add the marinated mutton and tomato and cook until the meat is browned and the oil separates.
Add 600ml water and cook 40 minutes until the mutton is tender and you have a strong stock.
Stir in the washed rice, mint, coriander and salt. Cover tightly and cook 15 minutes on the lowest heat.
steps.tip: The liquid should be roughly one and a half times the rice by volume, no more.

steps.text: Rest 10 minutes off the heat, squeeze over the lemon and fork through gently.

storage: Keeps 2 days refrigerated. Cool quickly and refrigerate within two hours, as with any cooked rice. Reheat with a sprinkle of water under a lid.
